query: Consider the following context: Temper embrittlement, characterized by a dramatic loss of ductility within a narrow temperature window, is ubiquitous in conventional alloys but is not reported in compositionally complex or high‐entropy alloy systems. In that context, which material can be used for ductile–brittle–ductile transition, and why?

decision.trend: Research has been focused on developing high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with improved mechanical properties, such as strength, ductility, and resistance to temper embrittlement. Various processing techniques, including arc melting, mechanical alloying, and spark plasma sintering, have been employed to produce HEAs with unique microstructures and phase compositions. The addition of alloying elements, such as Cr, has been shown to enhance the strength and ductility of HEAs. High-pressure and high-temperature treatment has also been used to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in HEAs.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made in developing HEAs, there is still a need to understand the underlying mechanisms that control their mechanical properties and to develop new processing techniques that can produce HEAs with consistent and reliable properties. Additionally, the effects of alloying elements and processing conditions on the microstructure and phase composition of HEAs need to be further investigated.
decision.why: Based on the trend of research in HEAs, the next step would be to investigate the effects of high-pressure and high-temperature treatment on the mechanical properties of HEAs. This treatment has been shown to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in HEAs, and further research is needed to understand the underlying mechanisms and to optimize the treatment conditions for different HEA compositions.
